title: Claude capability audit
tagline: Six months of Anthropic releases checked against every active repo: what we already use, what we're missing, and what's worth adopting first.
phase: Deadline fixes shipped; scheduled-agent decision next
bottomLine: All three deadline fixes shipped on 11 November. The shared skills library no longer names the retiring Sonnet 4.5. The eval study is pinned to a full model ID and a fixed CLI version. And four skills that loaded twice in every session now load once. Next is the biggest gain from the audit, the first scheduled cloud agent. It needs one decision from Alex by 18 November.
healthReason: Both risks that scored 6 of 9 cleared when the fixes merged. What's left has no deadline before the 30 November target except the runtime decision, which is two-way.
why: Diagnosis: Anthropic shipped new models, Claude Code features and API tools almost every week from May to November 2026, and nobody had checked them against the work in flight. The audit found that the system runs almost entirely inside Claude Code sessions, not through direct API calls. So the leverage is in agent tooling, and the exposure is in hard-coded model IDs.
mission: Inventory how each active repo uses Claude (models, Claude Code agents, skills and hooks, CI, direct API calls). Map the May–November 2026 release notes onto that inventory. Then rank what to change, by deadline first and by fit with current priorities second. Adopt a feature only when a named roadmap item needs it.
destination: Three conditions. No retired or retiring model is hard-coded anywhere. The eval study runs on a pinned model and CLI version. And one recurring job runs on a schedule as a cloud agent, instead of waiting for someone to start a session. Done when all three hold and every remaining idea is either adopted or explicitly dropped.
showcase: Treating the AI platform as a moving dependency: auditing releases against real usage instead of adopting features for their own sake
Ranking by deadline and risk first (a model retirement, a moving alias in a pre-registered study), then by fit with the roadmap
Checking the blast radius before deleting: finding the skill that referenced the copies being removed, and repointing it first
Saying what wasn't verified: release coverage after mid-September is partial, and the page says so

open.question: Where should the market-intel discovery loop run as a scheduled agent: a Claude Code routine, a Managed Agents scheduled deployment, or manual until the agent factory pilot?
open.unblocks: The first scheduled agent in the system, and the last condition in the definition of done.
open.recommendation: A Claude Code routine. It reuses the skills and connectors already in place and needs no new infrastructure. Move to Managed Agents only if the loop needs its own budget, or traces outside Claude Code.

open.question: Which beta API features (server-side message threads, on-demand compaction, per-message effort) earn a place in a build, and which wait for general availability?

decisions.decision: Keep the plugin repo as the single source for these skills, and delete the copies uploaded to claude.ai.
decisions.why: The claude.ai copies were one-time snapshots of the plugin with no review path, so they could only drift. Session history showed every real call went to the plugin copy.

decisions.decision: Ship the two deadline fixes as small pull requests right away, not through the agent factory gate.
decisions.why: Both were mechanical and time-boxed. Waiting on the factory's first phase would have put a 30 November deadline behind someone else's schedule.

risks.risk: A routine Claude Code update moves the CLI off the pinned version, and the eval runner stops sampling.
risks.mitigation: The runner fails closed, so no mixed data gets in. Hold the CLI at the pinned version for the study window (next step due 14 November).

risks.risk: Adopting features because they're new rather than because a project needs them.
risks.mitigation: Every adoption item names the roadmap item it serves. Anything that doesn't is dropped.

risks.risk: The release review is incomplete: Claude Code entries after mid-September are undated, and some app-side changes couldn't be confirmed from a primary source.
risks.mitigation: Unverified items stay off this page. The changelog is re-checked before each adoption.

assumptions.assumption: Agent definitions that name a model alias ('sonnet', 'opus') follow the current model and need no change.
assumptions.test: Check against the Claude Code model-configuration docs (next step due 21 November).

assumptions.assumption: A scheduled routine can use the same skills and connectors as an interactive session.
assumptions.test: Read the routines docs before the runtime decision on 18 November.

log.text: All three deadline fixes shipped: the retiring model ID replaced, the eval study pinned, and four duplicate skills removed after the one skill depending on them was repointed. Health moved to on track.

Audit done. Most of the system runs inside Claude Code sessions, not through direct API calls, so the biggest gains are in agent tooling. Two deadline items came first: a model retiring on 30 November, and the eval study's moving model alias.
